## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ec18b573e4ec5faaf342901675fa9356f294955e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md + none
Rule-change-verified: yes

Read: card #37921 (body, triage, claim 7221079945, os-dev-report 7221244862), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (one file, 10 lines added, none removed), and the check-runs on the head. Read but not reviewed: the rest of the skill on the head, `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` (Repeats, `summary`, replay) and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/eval.md` on `main`.

### ① Derived judgments

- No published surface, no schema, no accept set: the diff is 10 lines of prose in an internal skill (`metadata.internal: true`). Right.
- The one derived change is to what the eval seat may conclude: an iteration is no longer kept or dropped on one 5-run round. Right, and it is the change the card asks for.
- §3's "5 runs per config" for choosing a model or an effort is untouched by the hunk. Right.
- Check-runs on the head when read: every completed non-skipped run is `success` (Test Core, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lints, Type Check · workspace and debt ledger). Six runs were still `in_progress` (Lint · ESLint, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, CI/release/engine gates; Type Check · consumer gates, source gates). This record does not stand in for them: the queue reads their conclusions.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: `.claude/**` is not published, and `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. `Clause-②: no` is right: no authorable or published surface narrows or widens.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report carries no `open_questions`, no out-of-scope finding and `security_findings: none`. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- Dev flag "check:doc-formula-expressions exit 3, not measured locally, left to CI": answered by the head's check-runs, not by this record (see ①, still running when read).
- SQL push-down: not applicable, the diff holds no code.
- Rule change: the PR body declares `Rule-change: yes`. Verified against the diff: both bullets alter what gets done (how a round is graded into keep or drop, how "N consecutive rounds" is counted) and what goes to another seat (the overlap case is handed to the seat that dispatched the card). No `Ruling-ref:` is quoted, so it is `yes`, and the pull request waits for the maintainer.

### ④ Design judgment

`.claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md`, the two new bullets of §3.

Against the card's two items. Item 1 (a keep rule that names the spread it must exceed): answered. The unit is the round, the rule is "lowest round after above highest round before", both sides are also reported pooled. Item 2 ("N consecutive rounds" read by the same rule): answered in part, see S1.

Numbers. "64 and 59 on one tree, 5 points of 65": matches the card (r3 64, r4 59, same tree). "1/20": 3!·3!/6! = 36/720 = 1/20 for complete separation in the one named direction with three rounds a side and no real difference; correct as stated (see N1). The class example "6 wrong in 20 turns, 4 wrong in 30" is the card's own figure.

Against the card's rounds. Before 61, after 63, 64, 59: the sides overlap, so the text yields "inside the round-to-round spread" and neither keeps nor drops, which is what the same-tree 64/59 pair says the data can support. The before side has fewer than three rounds, so the rule also correctly says the comparison is not yet makeable. Tried to break it by optional stopping: adding rounds can only lower a side's minimum or raise its maximum, so more rounds never manufacture a "gain"; and §3's existing "no silent re-run, no outlier removal" line closes the pick-your-rounds route.

Followable with what exists. A round of 5 is one command with `--ask-repeats 5` (README, Repeats: the asks share one booted app, which is a further reason the round, not the single ask, is the right unit). Every command is recorded (§4), and `--driver recorded:FILE` re-scores ask turns with no model, honouring `--ask-repeats`; so "replay the old recordings first when the scorer changed" can be done. `summary` refuses to sum a replay with a live run and runs with different skill hashes; each side is one skill hash, and §3 already allows pooling by hand with the method stated, so pooling a replayed side is reachable.

Against the rest of the skill and pm-dispatch. No line of `pm-dispatch/**` reads eval rounds into a keep or a target decision; `lanes/eval.md` only requires a trend against the previous round, which the new text does not contradict. The hand-off "to the seat that dispatched the card" agrees with the lane boundary (the eval seat opens no PR and changes no skill text).

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — the "N consecutive rounds" bullet lets a miss be re-run away. "A round of the same tree that misses means not reached, and the count starts over" permits re-running the same tree until N rounds in a row pass, and the missed round then no longer counts against that tree. That is the single-lucky-reading failure the card is about, in a second place: a tree whose rounds read pass, miss, pass, pass, pass is "reached" under this bullet, while the keep rule one bullet above would take the same tree's lowest round as its reading. It is also not "the same rule". Fix on this prose face: a tree is reached only when every round run on that tree meets the target (N rounds or more, 15 runs or more); once a round of a tree misses, that tree is not reached on scores, and whether to add rounds or change the tree goes to the dispatching seat, as in the overlap case.

N1 (nit) — "1/20" holds exactly only without ties. Scores are integers near a ceiling of 65, ties are likely, and the rule demands strictly above, so the real chance is at most 1/20. "At most 1/20" would be exact.

N2 (nit) — the existing §3 line "compare only with the previous record" and §5's one record per round are not reconciled with a comparison that spans three or more records a side. Naming where the pooled reading is written (the newest record's Reading, citing each record it pools), and that the before tree may need two more rounds run now, would remove the guess.

N3 (nit) — "轮" in the new bullets means one 5-repeat run, while the skill's opening line defines a round as cards × configs × repetitions; and "the same tree" is not tied to a recorded stamp (`driver.askSkills` sha256, `template` sha256, `env.framework`). Naming the stamp would let a reader check "same tree" from the records.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), which earns a delta review of its fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-7qsbch-37921`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4df1893d234ef9c7d03c4e23108297252770b07a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md + none
Rule-change-verified: yes

Delta review of record 7221322040 (head `ec18b573`). Read: the delta diff `ec18b573..4df1893d` (one commit on top, the earlier head is its ancestor, one file), the net diff against `main` (one file, 12 lines added, none removed), the PR body as it stands, card #37921 and its comments (none new), and the check-runs on the new head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Still no published surface, no schema and no accept set: 12 lines of prose in an internal skill. Right.
- The delta narrows what the eval seat may conclude a second time: a target is reached only when every round run on a tree meets it. Right, and it is what S1 asked for.
- Check-runs on `4df1893d` when read: `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`. Still `in_progress`: Check PR Size, PR-body guards, filter, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, the three scoped lints (query-options erasure, slot lookup and corpus, tooling self-tests), and Type Check · workspace, consumer gates, source gates, debt ledger. Test Core, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate and Check Changeset had not reported a non-skipped run yet. This record does not stand in for any of them: the queue reads their conclusions.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `skip-changeset` and `Clause-②: no` are right for a `.claude/**` skill that is not published.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No new dev flag or `open_questions` entry on the card. SQL push-down: not applicable, no code.
- Rule change: the PR body declares `Rule-change: yes`. The delta hunks alter how a target is counted and add a second hand-off to the dispatching seat (more rounds or a new tree); no `Ruling-ref:` is quoted. It stays `yes`, and the pull request waits for the maintainer.
- The PR body still gives the first head's account: "10 lines", "the count starts over", "1 time in 20", and its runs block names head `ec18b573`. The tree is judged here, not the body, but the maintainer approves from that text; it should say what the tree now says before he reads it.

### ④ Design judgment

`.claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md`, §3, the delta against record 7221322040.

S1: closed. The bullet now reads: every round run on the same tree meets the target, N rounds or more and 15 runs or more, add rounds when short; one miss means not reached on scores, a re-run does not count it away, and more rounds or a new tree goes to the seat that dispatched the card. That is the keep rule's own reading of a side (its lowest round), so both bullets now treat a miss alike, and it agrees with §3's standing "no silent re-run, no outlier removal" line.

N1: closed ("at most 1/20"). N2: closed (the before tree is topped up now; the pooled reading goes in the newest record's Reading and names every record pooled; "compare only with the previous record" is scoped to the single-round trend, which leaves `lanes/eval.md`'s trend line intact). N3: closed (a round is one 5-repeat command; the same tree is named by recorded stamps).

New text against the rest of the skill, the runner README and `pm-dispatch/**`: no contradiction found. The three stamps exist where the text says (§5 already reads `driver.askSkills`, `template` and `env.framework` off the record). Requiring the same `env.framework` makes earlier rounds of a tree unusable once the runner commit moves; that is strict, not wrong, and "run the before tree now" covers it.

N4 (nit) — the definition of "the same tree" omits the package source. The rule covers iterations on tool descriptions, which ship in the packages; two rounds on different published versions with one runner commit share all three named stamps. The record carries `env.packagesLine`, and §1 already pins `--create-version` per round; naming that stamp as a fourth would close the gap. Left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up: a fix moves the head.

N5 (nit) — "一轮 = 一条 5 次重复的命令" fits a one-card set; on a set of several cards §1 runs one command per card, so a round is one such command per card. No effect on the card's case (one card).

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-7qsbch-37921`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 4df1893d23 · card #37921 · area s2-eval · 2026-11-27T15:03Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and checks.** 23 success, 24 expected skip, 0 failed on the head (the two failures on `ec18b573` are runs cancelled by the push). Draft, mergeable clean; 12 added lines in one file, `.claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md`; `skip-changeset` (the skill is not published).
- **Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** 7221322040 at `ec18b573`: PASS with S1 open (a missed round could be re-run away under "N consecutive rounds"). The delta record 7221375312 at this head: `S1: closed`, N1–N3 closed, `No must-fix, no should-fix.`; N4 (name the package source, `env.packagesLine`, in "same tree") and N5 (one command per card on a multi-card set) accepted as deviations and noted in the PR body. The transcript passes `verify-review-tier`. The seat adopts them.
- **What changes for an eval agent.** A skill iteration is kept only when, with at least 3 rounds and 15 runs a side on the same config, cards and scorer, the lowest round after the change is above the highest before it; the reverse drops it; any overlap is written "inside run-to-run spread" and decides nothing on scores, and more rounds or another reason to land go to the dispatching seat. "N consecutive rounds meet the target" needs every round run on that tree to meet it. On the #34996 rounds (before 61; after 63, 64, 59) this reads "inside the spread", as that card's ACCEPT stated.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Rule-change: yes` (verified `yes` by both records: it changes how rounds are graded and what goes to the seat; no ruling quoted). `Fixes #37921` is right: both items are answered.
- **Governance.** `.claude/**` with a rule change: Tier H. The maintainer's approval lands it.

Tier: H. Landing: hand-off to the maintainer follows this record.

## 维护者速读
- **改了什么：** 评测技能（scenario-eval）§3 加了两条判法。一是技能改动要不要保留：改前、改后每侧至少 3 轮、合计 15 次以上，同配置、同卡、同评分器；改后最低一轮高于改前最高一轮才算「提升」并保留，反过来算「回退」并丢弃；两侧有重叠就写「差别在轮间波动内」，不凭分数保留或丢弃，加不加轮交派卡席位。二是卡上写「连续 N 轮达标」：同一棵树上跑过的每一轮都要达标，有一轮没达标不能靠重跑数过去。
- **为什么：** #34996 那几轮里，同一棵树一轮 64、一轮 59，波动和要判的改动一样大，原来「一轮高于上一轮就保留」的做法分辨不出来。
- **影响：** 只改内部评测的判法，不改产品行为。以后迭代卡要多跑轮数才能说「提升」，成本会高一些；按新判法，#34996 那组分数读作「在波动内」，和那张卡 ACCEPT 时的说法一致。
- **审核：** 契约审核（最高档）第一轮 PASS，有一处建议改（漏掉的一轮可以靠重跑数过去），已修；增量复审 PASS（7221375312），没有必须改或建议改的项。席位 L1 ACCEPT 在本评论前一条。
- **要你做什么：** 这是规则改动（Rule-change: yes），需要你批准后才能合并。撤回这一次合并即恢复原样。
